parts.latex:
Given that $f(x)=\begin{cases}5-(x-3)^2, & x\le 2\\ mx+3, & x>2\end{cases}$

What is the value of $m$ for which $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=2$?

solutions.latex:
For $f$ to be continuous at $x=2$, the two pieces must agree at $x=2$:
$$\begin{aligned}5-(2-3)^2&=2m+3\\2m+3&=4\\2m&=1\\m&=\dfrac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
A function $f$ is given by the rule

$$f(x)=\begin{cases}(x-2)^2+1, & x\le 2\\ 4x-7, & x>2\end{cases}$$

What is the value of $f\Big(f(0)\Big)$?

solutions.latex:
Since $0\le2$, use the first rule:
$$f(0)=(0-2)^2+1=5$$
Since $5>2$, use the second rule:
$$f(5)=4(5)-7=13$$
